items.title: ‘Literally tasting the smoke’: Sarawakians suffer as haze worsens
items.summary: KUCHING, September 1 — Air quality in Malaysia's Sarawak state deteriorated further today as smoke from Indonesian forest fires drove up respiratory complaints and sent residents scrambling for protective masks. Six districts in Sarawak, on Borneo, recorded hazardous Air Pollutant Index (API) readings, including the state capital, Kuching, where the API hit 407. Mason said the worsening air had also affected her health, causing a sore throat and aggravating her asthma.

items.title: 5 arrested, others sought over viral Pudu nightclub brawl
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Five men with records for violent and drug-related offences have been arrested over a brawl outside a nightclub in Pudu, with police hunting for other suspects still at large. Wangsa Maju district police chief assistant commissioner Annas Sulaiman said the men, aged between 19 and 30, were believed to have been directly involved in the incident outside the nightclub. "Police also seized a black Perodua Myvi believed to have been used during the incident," he said in a statement today.

items.title: Teenager dies after touching lamp post in Bestari Jaya
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: A 15-year-old boy died after being electrocuted while touching a lamp post at a residential park in Taman Pancaran, Bestari Jaya, yesterday. Kuala Selangor police chief Superintendent Azaharudin Tajuddin said police received a call about the incident at 10.32pm. "The Kuala Selangor District Police Headquarters Operations Room received a call regarding a boy who was found unconscious and believed to be dead.

items.title: 4 arrested for allegedly robbing foreigners in Kodiang
items.summary: JITRA: Police have arrested four men believed to be involved in armed gang robberies targeting homes occupied by foreigners in the Kodiang area of Kedah. Kubang Pasu district police chief superintendent Mohd Radzi Abdul Rahim said the case came to light after a 28-year-old Myanmar national lodged a police report on Aug 17, claiming that his rented house in Kampung Kodiang Lama had been broken into by three masked men. He said police subsequently arrested four suspects aged between 22 and 37 at three locations, namely, Ipoh, Kodiang and Kangar.

items.title: KLCI faces fresh selling pressure as foreign outflows persist
items.summary: Kenanga Research said market sentiment was likely to remain cautious as investors digested hawkish remarks by US Federal Reserve chairman Kevin Warsh. The research house said the FBM KLCI fell 0.61 per cent, or 10.60 points week-on-week, to 1,725.88 points last week, as late-week profit-taking ahead of the extended Merdeka break outweighed earlier gains. HLIB Research said the KLCI had rallied 95 points from its year-to-date low of 1,655 points on June 29 to 1,753.20 points on Aug 26.

items.title: Missing Malaysian declared dead 2 years after swept away in India
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The High Court in Penang today declared Dr Balraj Sethi, who went missing after being swept away by strong currents in a river in India 2 years ago, dead. Suresh, who survived after being rescued by workers nearby, subsequently filed an application seeking a declaration of Balraj's death. The court also allowed Suresh to submit the court order to the Registrar for the registration of Balraj's death and the issuance of a presumed death certificate.

items.title: Between Us: Gen Z meets Gen Merdeka [WATCH]
items.summary: MERDEKA may have just been celebrated, but the history, memories and meaning behind Aug 31 continue to resonate across generations. That was the premise behind NST Between Us: Gen Z v Gen Merdeka, which brought together three young Malaysians and two veterans who were teenagers when Malaya achieved independence in 1957. They were Lt Col (Rtd) Datuk Zarazilah Mohamed Ali, 86; former Special Branch officer Datuk Paul Kiong, 82; Petaling Jaya councillor Loh Y Lun, 26; researcher Graciely Stefanie O'Hara, 26; and gap-year student Rajdev Sachdev Singh, 20.

items.title: Malaysia's resilience boosts appeal of government bonds
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's stable outlook and resilient fundamentals are expected to support foreign demand for government bonds, Malaysian Government Securities (MGS), MARC Ratings said. MARC Ratings said the outflow was largely driven by higher US Treasury yields, which increased the relative appeal of US government bonds. Malaysia's improving external position could also strengthen investor confidence.

items.title: Muhyiddin played golf at Tropicana on July 19, 2020, court told
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A witness told the High Court today that former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin was at the Tropicana Golf & Country Resort to play golf on July 19, 2020. Tropicana Golf & Country Resort Bhd (TGCRB) group head of security, S. Saravanan, 56, testified that a check on the Green Fee Tag showed Muhyiddin was among 15 players registered to play at the golf club that day. "Based on the Green Fee Tag, the players that day comprised four flights (groups) involving 15 players.

items.title: Israel PM's wife shares conspiracy theory about opposition figure
items.summary: JERUSALEM: Sara Netanyahu, the wife of the Israeli prime minister, has claimed an opposition figure was aware of the plan for Hamas's Oct 7, 2023 attack before it happened. In a television interview broadcast on Monday evening, Sara Netanyahu lashed out at Yair Golan, the former deputy military chief of staff who heads Israel's centre-left Democrats party. Sara Netanyahu's interview was broadcast on Israel's Channel 14, which is close to the government.

items.title: Former Tabung Haji chairman, ex-Treasury sec-gen released from MACC custody in RCI-linked probe
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 1 — A former Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) chairman and a former Treasury secretary-general were reportedly released from Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) custody today in an investigation linked to a royal commission of inquiry (RCI) report on the pilgrims’ fund. The politician and former TH chairman and the former Finance Ministry official were arrested at the MACC headquarters in Putrajaya on August 26. Before that, MACC detained seven people comprising a shipping company chief executive officer, two company directors and four former members of TH’s senior management.

items.title: Norway's new king to swear oath before parliament after Harald's death
items.summary: OSLO: King Haakon VIII of Norway will on Tuesday take an oath before parliament following the death of his father, pledging to uphold the Nordic country's constitution and laws in the latest in a series of ceremonies marking the passing of the crown. Haakon's father King Harald died on Friday at the age of 89. Haakon automatically became king the moment his father passed away.

items.title: Israel PM's wife shares conspiracy theory to boost husband's election chances
items.summary: TEL AVIV: Sara Netanyahu, the wife of the Israeli prime minister, has claimed an opposition figure was aware of the plan for Hamas's Oct 7, 2023 attack before it happened. In a television interview broadcast on Monday evening, Sara Netanyahu lashed out at Yair Golan, the former deputy military chief of staff who heads Israel's centre-left Democrats party. Sara Netanyahu's interview was broadcast on Israel's Channel 14, which is close to the government.

items.title: Ayer Itam brawl involved Geng 04 members in debt dispute, Penang police say
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 1 — Police have confirmed that an armed fight that caused two individuals to suffer severe injuries in front of a National Type Chinese Primary School in Ayer Itam here on Saturday involved Geng 04 members. Penang police chief Datuk Dennis Lim Kwang Keng said all 13 men arrested to facilitate investigations into the case are believed to be members of the same gang but in different areas and the fight was due to a misunderstanding over debts. He said the two severely injured men, in their 30s, were not gang members but were attacked when they were misidentified as suspects involved in the fight, adding the victims were on their way back from a religious festival when they were attacked by the group.

items.title: Three-year-old boy found dead below Victoria Bridge in Kuala Kangsar
items.summary: KUALA KANGSAR, Sept 1 — A three-year-old boy was reportedly found dead on a road beneath the Victoria Bridge in Enggor here yesterday evening. Sinar Harian reported that Abdul Rafee Abdul Halim was taken to Kuala Kangsar Hospital, where he was pronounced dead at about 7.40pm. The Kuala Kangsar Municipal Council subsequently cordoned off the bridge with safety tape.

items.title: Woman pleads guilty over RM17,300 baby transfer deal
items.summary: SUNGAI PETANI: A 24-year-old woman pleaded guilty in the Sessions Court today to an alternative charge of taking part in a transaction intended to permanently transfer control of a baby in exchange for RM17,300 last month. The court fixed Oct 5 for remention and sentencing. In a separate case at the magistrate's court, Kelsey also pleaded guilty to possessing another person's identity card last month.

items.title: Private helicopter deployed to search for 17 Malaysians missing in Nepal
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A private helicopter is being deployed today to search for 17 Malaysians who remain unaccounted for following flash floods in Nepal's Rasuwa district. Fishtail Tours & Travels representative Roshan Panday said he had arranged for the helicopter to search for the group at their last known location. "Today I am sending a helicopter privately.

items.title: Penang police arrest married couple, two others in drug syndicate on Thai intel tip
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 1 — Police have arrested four members of an international drug syndicate, including a married couple, and seized 86 kilogrammes of methamphetamine worth RM4.31 million in a series of raids in Selangor and Penang recently. Penang police chief Datuk Dennis Lim Kwang Keng said the success was the result of intelligence sharing between the Royal Malaysia Police and the Royal Thai Police after Thai authorities arrested a Malaysian man in Hua Hin, Thailand, on Aug 8. Thai narcotics police conducted an investigation and obtained intelligence, which was subsequently shared with the Malaysian Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department (NCID).

items.title: Nepal tragedy: Next of kin awaits call from authorities for DNA sample
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The next of kin of the victims who have still not been traced after the mudslide tragedy in Nepal a week ago are preparing to submit their deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) samples and are just waiting for a call from the authorities to do so. Sivakumar Kalimuthu, 57, husband of victim Kalai Mathe Karuppaiah, 57, said his children are now on standby and waiting for official notification to carry out the identity profile cross-reference procedure. Commenting further, Sivakumar said his wife was among the Malaysian citizens who were reported to be still missing while following an expedition to Mount Kailash in Tibet, China, before losing contact due to the natural disaster.

items.title: A family's four-day quest for a son lost in Nepal's floods ends
items.summary: FOR four agonising days after floodwaters tore through Nepal's Rasuwa district, Ayush Khadka's family searched desperately for any sign that the 21-year-old civil servant was still alive. Ayush had spoken to relatives the night before the flood, and his social media account even appeared to show him as online the following morning, a small sign that gave the family hope he had survived. Despite repeatedly sharing Ayush's name, workplace and last known location in Timure with officials, the family received few answers, Ganesh said.

items.title: Motorcyclist killed, another seriously hurt in four-vehicle crash [WATCH]
items.summary: Penang Fire and Rescue Department operations assistant director John Sagun Francis said the 1.04pm crash at Km127.4 involved 2 motorcycles and 2 Perodua Myvi cars. John said two occupants of the Perodua Myvi cars escaped unhurt. Six firefighters, including the operations commander, were involved in the rescue operation, with 1 Light Fire Rescue Tender deployed.

items.title: Duta Enclave: Court told RM1.39m payout to Semantan Estate was more than adequate
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, September 1 — The High Court was told today that the RM1.39 million in compensation paid by the Government of Malaysia to Semantan Estate (1952) Sdn Bhd for the acquisition of 263.272 acres of land, known as the Duta Enclave, in 1956 was more than adequate. “I have prepared an expert valuation report to determine adequate compensation, in accordance with the Court of Appeal Order dated June 24, 2025, which, among others, fixed the valuation date for determining compensation for the said land as December 3, 1956. “Given that the government had previously paid compensation of $1,390,602.70 (in 1956) to the plaintiff (Semantan Estate), that amount exceeds the compensation I recommended under Valuation Basis 1.

items.title: DNA samples from family of missing Malaysian in Nepal floods to be taken tomorrow
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: DNA samples from the next of kin of a Malaysian who remains missing following devastating floods in Nepal will be collected tomorrow. Tomorrow, they will take DNA samples from the next of kin," she said briefly via WhatsApp. Meanwhile, the Foreign Ministry said 55 Malaysians remained unaccounted for following flash floods and landslides in Nepal's Rasuwa district.

items.title: New coffee festival set to solidify Ipoh's identity as iconic 'Coffee City'
items.summary: IPOH: The diverse coffee drinking culture of the country's multi-racial community, alongside elements of food, music, art and tourism, will enliven the Ipoh Coffee Vibes 2026 Festival which will be held for four days at the Riverfront Old Town Ipoh next to Jalan Sultan Iskandar here. Loh said the Ipoh Coffee Vibes Festival 2026 would not only highlight white coffee but also bring together coffee cultures of various races and styles, including special coffees from the Malay community, Indian kopi tarik, international brands Starbucks as well as various snacks, desserts and foods themed with coffee or suitable for enjoying with coffee. Loh said at the same time, participating coffee entrepreneurs would introduce 'Kopi Rakyat' specifically for the Ipoh Coffee Vibes Festival to allow the public to enjoy various types and flavours of coffee at more consumer-friendly prices.

items.title: EU frets over Kyiv's defences, 'hybrid' threat from Moscow
items.summary: WICKLOW: EU defence and foreign ministers gathering in Ireland from Tuesday will grapple with bolstering Ukraine's air defences amid growing worries over Russia's campaign to destabilise Kyiv's European backers. Moscow has taken advantage of Ukraine running low on US-built air defence missiles to pummel the country, while Kyiv has hit back against Russian infrastructure with its own long-range strikes. Defence ministers – who meet Tuesday before foreign ministers hold talks Wednesday – are expected to speak with Ukraine's new acting defence minister Yevgeniy Khmara.

items.title: Japan arrests man twice for hamster massacres
items.summary: TOKYO: Police in Japan said Tuesday they had arrested a man over the killing of 30 hamsters at a hotel, weeks after he was detained for stomping to death 20 others. The 36-year-old high school staffer in the northern region of Iwate teamed up with two different women at so-called "love hotels" – short-stay lodging meant for couples – where he allegedly killed hamsters in violation of animal protection laws, police told AFP. The two women have also been arrested, said Hiroyuki Nasu, a senior police official in the city of Miyako, Iwate.

items.title: Saifuddin Nasution expresses appreciation to marine police on its 79th anniversary
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail expressed his appreciation to the marine police force in conjunction with its 79th anniversary celebration today. He said that since its establishment 79 years ago, the force has stood firm in safeguarding the country's waters, defending the nation's sovereignty and protecting the people's interests. "Behind every patrol and operation lies the bravery, discipline and sacrifice of our marine police personnel, who are always prepared to face any challenges to ensure the country's waters remain peaceful and protected.

items.title: Home Ministry developing framework for CCFC establishment next year
items.summary: IPSOM deputy chief executive SAC Dr Shazrin Azlin Ruslan said the initiative was a continuation of the National Cybercrime Threat Action Plan study undertaken by IPSOM in collaboration with Cyber Security Academia Malaysia (CSAM) and local universities last year. She said the local universities involved in the study were Universiti Sains Islam Malaysia (USIM), Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia (UKM), Universiti Putra Malaysia (UPM) and Universiti Teknologi Mara (UiTM). She said the study on the establishment of the CCFC had identified 47 types of cyber-enabled crimes and 10 types of cyber-dependent crimes from the Home Ministry's perspective.

items.title: Former PM Muhyiddin, ‘Azman’ and ‘Adam’ listed in same July 2020 golf game at Tropicana, witness tells court
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 1 — Former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin played in a golf game in July 2020 at Tropicana Golf Club with 14 other players, including two individuals identified as “Azman” and “Adam”, Tropicana Golf & Country Resort Berhad (TGCRB) employee Saravanan Subaramaniam told the High Court today. TGCRB group head of security Saravanan said this while testifying as the 28th prosecution witness in Muhyiddin’s power abuse and money laundering trial. Saravanan said Tropicana Golf Club’s digital golf registration system showed that Muhyiddin and the 14 other individuals had played there in four “flights”, or groups, on July 19, 2020, with a single invoice issued for all 15 players.

items.title: Cross-Border Insolvency Act enhances legal certainty, safeguards creditors and stakeholders
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The enforcement of the Cross-Border Insolvency Act 2026 (Act 877), which came into force on Aug 28, will enhance the efficiency of cross-border insolvency case management. Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said and Minister of Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali said the Act also improves legal certainty and protects the interests of creditors and stakeholders. "Act 877 provides a dedicated mechanism for handling insolvency proceedings involving debtors, assets, creditors, or proceedings in more than one jurisdiction.

items.title: King, Queen attend Johor Super Crown Tournament 2026
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: His Majesty, Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia and Her Majesty Raja Zarith Sofiah, Queen of Malaysia attended the Johor Super Crown Tournament (JSCPT) 2026 at Istana Pasir Pelangi, here today. Also attending the event was the Regent of Johor Tunku Mahkota Ismail. The tournament will run from today until Sept 6, bringing together five world-class teams lined up with elite international players, namely Royal Johor, Temasek, Korea Polo, J-Corp and Digital Bridge.

items.title: Duta Enclave: Court told RM1.39mil govt payout to Semantan Estate more than adequate
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The High Court was told today that the RM1.39 million in compensation paid by the Government of Malaysia to Semantan Estate (1952) Sdn Bhd for the acquisition of 263.272 acres (106.544ha) of land, known as the Duta Enclave, in 1956 was more than adequate. "I have prepared an expert valuation report to determine adequate compensation, in accordance with the Court of Appeal Order dated June 24, 2025, which, among others, fixed the valuation date for determining compensation for the said land as Dec 3, 1956. "Given that the government had previously paid compensation of $1,390,602.70 (in 1956) to the plaintiff (Semantan Estate), that amount exceeds the compensation I recommended under Valuation Basis 1.

items.title: Juwai IQI: Malaysia among top destinations for Chinese property buyers, investment on track to top RM1.6b a year
items.summary: According to new insights released today by Juwai IQI, the profile of Chinese buyers in Malaysia is undergoing a significant transformation. “Malaysia is now the fourth most popular destination for Chinese property buyers, up from sixth in 2025 and from seventh in 2022, 2023, and 2024,” Kashif said. In 2024, Malaysia attracted 2.8 per cent of global property enquiries from Chinese homebuyers, with the figure climbing to 4.5 per cent in 2025.

items.title: 3-year-old boy dies after falling through gap on Victoria Bridge
items.summary: SUNGAI SIPUT: A 3-year-old boy died after falling five metres from Victoria Bridge in Enggor here yesterday. District police chief Superintendent Charan Ai Wan said the victim was walking on the historical bridge with his 42-year-old father when the incident happened. He said the victim, from Kluang, Johor, was visiting Victoria Bridge on a family holiday.

items.title: Air Itam clash involved rival factions of 04 gang, police confirm
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Police have confirmed that the recent violent clash in Air Itam involved members of the 04 gang operating independently under separate factions. State police chief Datuk Dennis Lim said the 04 name was being used by distinct groups operating in different areas for their own interests. Lim said the incident stemmed from a debt dispute, with one group attempting to collect money owed on behalf of another party.

items.title: Tanjung Bungah dog attack: MBPP cancels licence, issues RM250 compound
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: The Penang Island City Council (MBPP) has cancelled a dog licence and issued its owner a RM250 compound following an attack on a stray dog in Tanjung Bungah. Mayor Datuk A. Rajendran said the action was taken under the Muncipal Council of Penang Island Dogs Bylaws following the incident, which went viral on social media. The incident in Tanjung Bungah sparked public concern after footage of the dog attacking a stray was widely circulated on social media.

items.title: UNHCR warns Myanmar remains unsafe for refugees to return
items.summary: The Home Ministry said last week it had finalised the first phase of a voluntary repatriation programme that will see 1,476 refugees returned to Myanmar on September 29. Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim had earlier said Myanmar had agreed to repatriate 5,000 Rohingya, amid rising tensions over the refugees within local communities in Malaysia. The UNHCR said an ongoing armed conflict and violence across Myanmar meant there could not be a safe, dignified and sustainable voluntary return of refugees.

items.title: RM1bil additional micro-financing should come with faster approval: FMM
items.summary: FMM president Jacob Lee Chor Kok said the move was important as small and medium enterprises (SMEs) continue to face pressure from rising operating costs and cash flow constraints. "The government should also ensure adequate access to financing for eligible small manufacturers and manufacturing-related businesses. Lee also said that FMM recognises the government's decision to introduce measures that can provide more immediate support as businesses continue to contend with operating cost pressures, cash-flow constraints and an increasingly challenging and competitive business environment.

items.title: Perak assembly to choose new senator between PKR and PAS nominees
items.summary: IPOH, Sept 1 — The upcoming Perak State Legislative Assembly sitting will see a motion tabled to elect a new senator, Speaker Datuk Seri Mohammad Zahir Abdul Khalid said. Mohammad Zahir said the motion would be tabled by Mentri Besar Datuk Seri Saarani Mohamad. He also said two Bills would be tabled during the sitting, namely the Administrative Members and State Assembly Members (Salary) Enactment 2026 and the Islamic Religious Administration (Perak) (Amendment) Enactment 2026.

items.title: Deadly LPT1 pile-up: Four dead include family returning from National Day parade in Putrajaya
items.summary: Mohd Kazwan Mohd Kassim, 59, the father of one of the victims, Nur Atiqah Sofiya, 32, said it was the first time his daughter, her husband, Muhammad Nazatul Nazmi, 32, and their son, Muhammad Armaan Nazeef, four, had celebrated National Day in Putrajaya. Meanwhile, the victim’s cousin, Nur Awatif Adawiyah Abdul Aziz, 30, said Nur Atiqah Sofiya had sent photos of the National Day celebrations to the family’s WhatsApp group and also uploaded photos to her Instagram Story. We never thought these photos would become their last memories,” she said.

items.title: Court of Appeal allows Rosmah to introduce new evidence in solar graft appeal
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 1 — The Court of Appeal today allowed applications by former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s wife, Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor, to adduce additional evidence in her appeal against her corruption conviction, paving the way for the evidence to be heard by the High Court. A three-member panel comprising Justices Choo Kah Sing, Azhahari Kamal Ramli and K. Muniandy allowed both applications before it and ordered that the additional evidence be taken before another High Court judge. Justice Choo, who read the panel’s decision, said the court was satisfied that the requirements for admitting the additional evidence had been met.

items.title: Sabah disaster committee urges public to limit outdoor activities as four districts record unhealthy API
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 1 — The Sabah State Disaster Management Committee (JPBN) has urged the public, particularly vulnerable groups, to limit outdoor activities and avoid strenuous physical exertion after four locations across the state recorded unhealthy air pollutant index (API) levels today. The committee issued the advisory as hazy conditions shrouded several districts, calling on children, senior citizens, pregnant women, and individuals suffering from respiratory illnesses to exercise extra caution. The advisory comes as data from the Sabah Department of Environment (DOE) showed air quality worsening across multiple monitoring stations as of 8am today.

items.title: Islamic affairs minister denounces Malaysian’s participation in Bangkok transgender pageant
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 1 — The Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) has strongly condemned the participation of an individual, allegedly representing Malaysia, in a transgender beauty pageant held in Bangkok last Sunday. “Religious authorities will work with the relevant agencies to examine possible action under existing laws,” he said. Earlier, a video showing an individual representing Malaysia at an international transgender beauty pageant went viral on social media, drawing mixed reactions from netizens.

items.title: ‘Baddestcoach’ defamation suit against Caprice heads to trial after settlement talks collapse
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 1 — The defamation suit filed by renowned high-performance transformation coach Syed Mohammad Murad Syed Naseem, better known as Murad “Baddestcoach” Zaidi, against social media influencer Caprice will proceed to full trial following the failure of both parties to reach an amicable settlement at the High Court here. He added that the mediation proceedings, which took place on July 31 and lasted nearly four hours, were attended by both Caprice, whose real name is Ariz Ramli, and Murad Zaidi. On Nov 8 last year, the High Court recorded a consent order compelling Caprice to immediately remove and withdraw nine defamatory statements published on his Instagram account against Murad Zaidi.

items.title: Sarawak electoral boundary redelineation: 17 new seats proposed, 10 renamed
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 1 — Seventeen new state constituencies have been proposed across Sarawak under the Election Commission’s (EC) 2026 electoral boundary review, with Petra Jaya, Sibu, and Miri parliamentary constituencies each set to gain two new seats. Miri would also gain two new constituencies through the proposed Permaisuri and Tudan. In addition, the EC has proposed changes to the names of 10 state constituencies.

items.title: No changes to Perak Opposition seating despite Bersatu fallout, says Speaker
items.summary: IPOH, Sept 1 — The Perak State Assembly has not received any formal request to alter the Opposition’s seating arrangement following recent sackings and suspensions within Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (Bersatu), Speaker Datuk Seri Mohammad Zahir Abdul Khalid said today. In June, Sungai Manik assemblyman Datuk Zainol Fadzi Paharudin announced his entry into Parti Wawasan Negara (Wawasan), four months after his expulsion from Bersatu. Zainol Fadzi was among 17 members sacked nationwide by Bersatu over alleged party sabotage.

items.title: Penang DVS: No clear offence under Animal Welfare Act for owner failing to stop dog fight
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 1 — The Animal Welfare Act 2015 contains no clear provision making it an offence for a dog owner to fail to intervene when dogs fight, the Penang Veterinary Services Department (DVS) has said. “There is no clear provision under the Act that (makes it) an offence by an owner for an animal fight or for failing to stop the fight,” DVS was quoted as saying. However, it said action could be considered under Section 8 of the Minor Offences Act 1955 if there was evidence that someone had encouraged or prompted an animal to attack, alarm or frighten another person or animal.

items.title: Merdeka break expected to bring RM36m to southern Thailand from 60,000 Malaysian tourists
items.summary: KOTA BARU, Sept 1 — About 60,000 Malaysians are expected to spend an estimated RM36 million in southern Thailand during the five-day Merdeka Day and school holiday period. The New Straits Times reported Thailand-Asean Halal Trade and Tourism Association president Aida Oujeh as saying the estimate covered travellers entering the country from August 29 to September 2. “The main destinations are Hat Yai, Phatthalung, Satun, Betong, Bangkok and Krabi.

items.title: Johari Ghani: US forced labour issue resolved, excess capacity still pending
items.summary: He said the investigation is close to being finalised, while Malaysia continues to engage with the US on the definition of excess capacity. “They have almost finalised the excess capacity investigation. Johari said Malaysia’s concern is that the US definition of excess capacity also takes into account capacity originating from third countries.

items.title: MOF: Budi95 and Budi Diesel monthly entitlements back to 300L today
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 1 — The basic monthly eligibility limit under Budi Madani has been increased from 200 to 300 litres, effective today. The Ministry of Finance (MOF), in a Facebook post, said the adjustment covers Budi Madani RON95 (Budi95) and Budi Madani Diesel (Budi Diesel), with eligible recipients entitled to up to 300 litres monthly. The additional allocation raises the monthly entitlement for eligible private diesel pick-up truck and jeep owners from 300 to 400 litres from today.

items.title: Boy awarded RM359,123 after botched circumcision leaves permanent scarring
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 1 — A Terengganu Sessions Court has reportedly awarded RM359,122.90 to a boy who suffered permanent scarring and extensive skin loss following a botched circumcision at a private clinic in 2023. The New Straits Times reported that Judge Wan Nor Aklima Wan Salleh awarded RM300,000 in general damages and RM59,122.90 in special and future damages after finding Klinik Perubatan Hijraa in Kuala Nerus medically negligent. The boy suffered serious genital injuries that required prolonged hospital treatment and further surgery, including full-thickness skin grafting.

items.title: Zahid Hamidi directs Rural Development Ministry to clear backlog by year-end
items.summary: Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Rural and Regional Development Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the move was important given that the time remaining until 2026 is not long, besides the cost of a problem would increase if decisions were further delayed. Ahmad Zahid said a comprehensive review should be carried out this month covering all projects, payments, land issues, utilities, contracts, assets and decisions that have not yet been resolved. “My principle is simple: No issue without an owner, no project without a timeline, no meeting without a decision,” he said.

items.title: Dead fish and crabs raise pollution concerns in Sitiawan river, DOE investigates
items.summary: IPOH, Sept 1 — Environmental group Persatuan Aktivis Sahabat Alam (Kuasa) has raised concerns over alleged river pollution in Kampung Sitiawan, Manjung, after photographs and videos shared on social media showed dead fish and crabs. Kuasa said in a statement that it received complaints about the incident yesterday morning through social media posts shared by members of the public. The group said two separate posts included photographs and videos that it claimed provided clear evidence of pollution in the river and the deaths of aquatic species.

items.title: NRD: MyKad printing services disrupted until Sept 7 for shift to new-gen
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 1 — The National Registration Department (NRD) is transitioning from the existing MyKad structure to the new-generation MyKad, causing temporary disruptions to its printing services. In a statement today, the NRD announced that the printing disruption is expected to last from today through Sept 7. JPN also expressed its appreciation for the public’s patience and cooperation throughout this transitional period.

items.title: National Day secretariat: Automatic invitations for ex-PMs stopped since 2018
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 1 — Official invitations to National Day celebrations are not automatically extended to former prime ministers based on the set practice since 2018, the National Day Celebration 2026 Secretariat said yesterday. The secretariat issued the clarification after questions were raised about former prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad’s attendance at yesterday’s celebration at Dataran Putrajaya. “Based on the practice since 2018, invitations to the National Day Celebration are not automatically extended to former prime ministers.

items.title: Haze in Malaysia: Why burning leaves and rubbish in your compound is more dangerous than you think
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 1 — Small-scale burning activities such as burning rubbish, leaves and dry branches in residential yards, which are often considered trivial, can contribute to local air pollution, experts said. Aweng said that during haze conditions such as those currently affecting the country, open burning could further increase the concentration of pollutants in an area, particularly when air circulation is poor. Under the current haze conditions, open burning will further increase the concentration of pollutants in the area,” he said.

items.title: Three killed as Proton Aeroback plunges into ravine on Lahad Datu forest road
items.summary: LAHAD DATU, Sept 1 — Three men were killed and another injured after the car they were travelling in skidded before plunging into a ravine on Jalan Hutan Simpan Bagahak, here yesterday. Lahad Datu Fire and Rescue Station chief Sumsoa Rashid said his department received an emergency call regarding the incident at 7.38 pm before the team arrived at the location at 8.16 pm. “Another adult male sustained injuries and was sent to hospital using a MOH ambulance for further treatment,” he said in a statement.

items.title: Sarawak haze crisis: Kuching API hits 407, six areas in hazardous zone
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 1 — Six areas in Sarawak recorded Air Pollutant Index (API) readings at the hazardous level as of 8 am today, with the Serian District Police Headquarters recording the highest reading at 408. Three areas in Sarawak recorded readings at the very unhealthy level – Mukah (234), Bintulu (232) and Samalaju (225). Forty-eight areas nationwide were reported to have moderate API readings.

items.title: Dear Malaysia: Our shared beloved home
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 1 — Selamat Hari Kebangsaan and Selamat Hari Malaysia , my dear fellow Malaysians. Each year, I reflected on the many challenges facing our beloved nation; our economy, education, corruption, political reforms, climate change, artificial intelligence and the rapidly changing world around us. Many of us become husbands and wives.

items.title: Fatal LPT1 accident: Four dead in 11-vehicle crash near Kuantan
items.summary: KUANTAN, Sept 1 — Four people were killed in an accident involving 11 vehicles at KM110 of the East Coast Expressway 1 (LPT1) from Lanchang towards Kuantan yesterday. Pahang Fire and Rescue Department operations assistant director Mohd Salahuddin Isa said the department received an emergency call at 10.44 pm. He said those killed were trapped in two vehicles.
